While the underlying MM framework theoretically guarantees monotonic increase if the surrogate function is maximized exactly, the paper employs approximate off-the-shelf solvers (RRWM, MGM-Floyd) in the practical implementation. By not explicitly acknowledging that the *practical* implementation loses the strict convergence guarantee, the authors misrepresent the theoretical robustness of their solution.

Furthermore, the claim that the method "outperforms supervised models" is presented too broadly. While true for the clean Willow dataset, the same UM3C method lags significantly behind supervised BBGM on the more challenging Pascal VOC dataset (MA 0.498 vs 0.792). This, combined with the lack of statistical significance reporting (standard deviations/error bars) and unspecified pseudo-label update schedules, weakens the credibility of the experimental claims.

Despite these issues, the paper makes a genuine and valuable contribution. The decoupled affinity learning mechanism is clean and effective, and the empirical gains are real, even if the "supervised beating" narrative needs refinement.
